sn22.88:1.2: Not to be confused with the shameless Assaji of [mn70:4.1](), this is probably the early disciple of that name ([mn35:3.1]()). Assaji was one the group of five mendicants who received the Buddha’s first discourse ([pli-tv-kd1:6.36.1]()). Shortly afterwards he inspired Sāriputta with a classic epitome of the teaching ([pli-tv-kd1:23.2.1]()).
sn22.88:3.10: This is possibly in reference to Godhika, who likewise was distressed by his inability to keep up his meditation ([sn4.23:1.4]()). States of _samādhi_ are conditioned and dependent on a healthy body, which is why the Bodhisatta needed to eat before he became enlightened ([mn36:33.2]()). The Buddha urges final Nibbana, which is not a state of consciousness, but freedom from attachment.
sn22.88:3.11: The notion that even an arahant can decline is discussed and rejected at [kv1.2]().
